Build the calibration report

Source: R/project_report.R
build_report.Rd

Writes a report generated entirely from the log: never edit it by hand, rebuild it. The HTML file is self-contained, with its figures embedded, so it can be emailed or attached to a review. A Markdown copy with separate figure files suits projects kept under version control.

Usage

build_report(
  project,
  output = file.path(project, "report"),
  rerun = TRUE,
  sensitivity = NULL,
  sensitivity_range = 0.5,
  sensitivity_steps = 9L
)

Arguments

project

Path of a calibration project folder.

output

Folder to write to; created if needed.

rerun

If TRUE, the integrity section reruns every logged run.

sensitivity

TRUE, FALSE, or NULL for on when the latest candidate has been validated, which is when a Steward reviews the project.

sensitivity_range, sensitivity_steps

Range of the multiplicative variation and the number of points per parameter.

Value

The path of report.html, invisibly.

Details

Sections, in reading order: project and roles; integrity (any failure is flagged at the top); data and scoring windows; model structure; the calibration path, as a tree of runs and a table of every run with its changes, scores, verdict and reasoning; the candidate, with hydrographs, flow-duration curves and a scatter for both windows; parameter sensitivity; sign-off history; and an appendix with the final configuration and the entry checksums.

Sensitivity varies each nonzero numeric parameter of the candidate, one at a time, by factors from 1 - sensitivity_range to 1 + sensitivity_range, and scores the headline metric on the calibration window. A flat curve means the data do not determine that parameter. It costs sensitivity_steps model runs per parameter.

See also

calibration_log, verify_project()
